title: A man in a real fight: blind fire from cover, and a man down at zero G on his boots, on the stage and on his target card
about: v0.0.27, "Away the boarding party", puts armed men who are not role-players on the Patient Mule's deck 2 at zero G, each on locked mag boots, and live rounds both ways. An irregular in cover may fire blind: the rifle over or round his cover, his head below it, FIRING BLIND. A man hit hangs from his locked boots where he stood: there is no floor to fall to, DOWN. The stage has no frame for either today (a man in cover kneels at the low ready; a man down sits where he is), so these are the candidates. Every picture is the game's own code: a holdout in the game's Belt coverall (the dress is the belt-crew set's to score; here its blue-grey make), no carrier, no mask, the R-7, composed at the stage's 16 px/m by the figure engine with the candidate's pose, shaded and snapped to the palette as the stage draws him, on the hauler's deck plate and three times his size: first what the stage draws today, then the candidate toward you, away, side on to the right and to the left, and a man down also on the deckhead, toward you and away, turned as the stage turns a body there. Under them his target card: today's, then the candidate's at 4 m and 14 m, in the same coverall. B (the default B-a) is blind fire; Z (the default Z-a) is a man down at zero G. The game builds the defaults until you score; each pick is one row of the figure's poses (a band of the stance pool, beside the daze and the cower) and one of the card's.

open.decides: how a holdout firing blind from cover (B) and a man down at zero G on his locked boots (Z) are drawn on the stage and on his target card in Away the boarding party
